agent.name: Promethean Technology Classification Agent
agent.specialty: Technology significance and bounded application implications

analytical_question: How significant are indoor autonomous delivery robots, and should the hypothetical large restaurant authorize a controlled meal-delivery pilot?
general_et_finding: Prospective classification: Breakthrough, with moderate confidence, relative to manual carrying or pushing a cart. The unit is a complete indoor wheeled navigation-and-delivery system, not a sensor, a new cosmetic model feature, or all robotics. E2-E3 report a meaningful capability: completing bounded transport routes without a human escorting every trip. This is a course-based interpretation of supplier capability evidence, not measured 10x productivity. Candidate barrier: in a conventional table-running workflow, a person accompanies the carried meal. That workflow constraint is reduced; it is not a universal historical barrier, because automated transport already existed. Physical distance, route suitability and handoff responsibilities remain. Suppressing this robot class would plausibly restore human carrying and carts, not cause established cross-tier infrastructure collapse; this is a reasoned counterfactual, not an observed shutdown. Restaurant and hotel delivery mainly concern the economic tier. No categorical dissolution across biological survival and cognitive/social life is established. E1 therefore does not support Potential Promethean. The dissolution gate fails, so six-criterion scoring is NOT REACHED. Diagnostic gaps are: defined 10x gain, broad cross-tier impact, civilizational paradigm shift, dependent innovation wave, expanded access across groups, and irreversible dependence. The bounded autonomous task is more than a faster manual cart, while the local use can still be an incremental workflow improvement.
application_finding: Kitchen-to-table transport is an incremental restaurant workflow improvement. A robot can carry a batch toward a handoff point, while staff load food, complete service, handle exceptions and support diners. Reduced walking is not evidence that a whole server role disappears.
organization_specific_finding: The large restaurant is a moderate/fast-follower. Flat dry flooring, an approximately 1.2 m route before crowding, charging space and a trained supervisor are hypothetical assumptions. They support a vendor route assessment and bounded trial, not a finding that the venue is already safe or profitable. E2's clearance specification is not a crowd-flow or turning assessment.
contrary_evidence_or_limitations: E4 documents continued human oversight and physical operating limits for another model; these are counterevidence to unrestricted autonomy, not universal numerical rules.
Most capability evidence is supplier-authored, with no independent site benchmark or local cost outcome.
Physical transport and manual fallback remain; multiple hospitality settings do not establish multiple dissolved tiers.
confidence_and_uncertainty: Moderate confidence in Breakthrough as a bounded system-level capability change relative to manual carrying. Local net value and operational suitability are unknown. A minor improvement to an existing delivery robot could instead be incremental; this finding concerns the complete autonomous-delivery capability, not every product revision.
value_opportunity_implication: Potentially reduce repetitive walking and free attention for service, only if loading, unloading, supervision and interventions do not absorb the saved time. No headcount reduction or payback is established.
risk_governance_implication: Keep a trained shift supervisor accountable for operation, vendor-approved routes and configuration, controlled handoff, incident logging and manual fallback. Check pedestrian access and hot-item handling before live use; this specialist does not certify safety.
recommendation_management_implication: First complete a vendor and venue route assessment. If acceptable, run a four-week controlled pilot without reducing staffing. Proposed evaluation: compare robot-assisted and manual delivery on 30 matched meal runs across comparable service periods. Record total human minutes per completed run, including loading, handoff, monitoring and rescue; end-to-end completion time; failed runs; interventions; spills; and access conflicts. The shift supervisor owns the log. Proposed expansion gate: lower total human effort with service time no worse than the manual baseline and no unresolved safety or access problem. Pause on a collision, spill with injury risk, blocked essential access, or recurring unhandled route failure; return to manual delivery. These are proposed management gates, not validated statistical thresholds or observed results.
change_monitoring_triggers: Reassess pilot scope on measured total effort, delivery completion, interventions, service time, cost and incidents.
Reconsider the broad classification only on evidence of categorical barrier dissolution across multiple tiers and durable infrastructure dependence; publicity alone does not qualify.
Review broad significance annually over three years and refresh product-specific evidence before procurement.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Obtain actual route, turning, crowding and handoff assessment before live use.
Withhold a safe-deployment guarantee, quantified ROI and a staffing-replacement claim without local evidence.
Withhold Potential or Confirmed Promethean on the supplied evidence.

evidence.claim: E1: Chapter 11 distinguishes constraint reduction from categorical dissolution and requires the system, suppression and tier tests.
evidence.source_or_reference: Fortino, Chapter 11, Identifying Promethean Technologies, August 2026 draft Rev 0.1, sections 11.2 and 11.7, pp. 3-4 and 8-11; supplied course PDF.
evidence.notes: Conceptual lens, not empirical performance evidence.

evidence.claim: E2: PUDU describes BellaBot Pro delivery modes, obstacle sensing and a 65 cm path-clearance specification.
evidence.notes: Supplier claim, not independent safety or ROI evidence. The page labels dish recognition and broadcast as under development; do not treat that feature as deployed.

evidence.claim: E3: PUDU reports a FlashBot elevator-integration test with Nippon Otis.
evidence.notes: Historical supplier report, not proof of compatibility with an arbitrary hotel elevator or independent long-run service performance.

evidence.claim: E4: The Servi Plus manual requires operating-space checks, mapping, human handoff and monitoring during peak periods.
evidence.notes: Read safety and use sections, printed pp. 6, 10, 16 and 19. Model-specific limits do not transfer automatically to PUDU products; supports a bounded example of continuing human responsibilities.

evidence.claim: E5: Nav2 documentation explains how robot footprint and local navigation configuration affect passage through space.
evidence.notes: General technical illustration, not proof that either named robot uses Nav2 or is safe in a specific venue.
